blocks.content: Tribunals are quasi-judicial bodies bound by the principles of natural justice, designed to ensure speedy and specialized adjudication without being tied down by rigid procedural technicalities.

rows: Broad and general jurisdiction over civil and criminal matters
Specialized jurisdiction restricted to specific administrative or statutory subjects
Strictly governed by CPC, CrPC, and Indian Evidence Act
Guided by Principles of Natural Justice, free from strict evidence rules
Presided over purely by trained judicial officers and judges
Comprises both judicial members and technical/administrative experts
Possesses inherent powers vested by the State's judicial system
Possesses only statutory powers conferred by the specific establishing Act

items: Article 323A allows ONLY Parliament to establish administrative tribunals, whereas Article 323B allows both Parliament and State Legislatures to establish tribunals for specific subjects.
In the landmark L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India (1997) case, the Supreme Court held that judicial review under Articles 226/227 by High Courts is part of the basic structure of the Constitution.
Tribunals do not possess inherent judicial powers like traditional courts; their jurisdiction is strictly limited to what is conferred by the establishing statute.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Courts are traditional judicial bodies possessing inherent judicial powers of the State, whereas tribunals are quasi-judicial bodies created by statute for specialized matters.
Courts are strictly bound by procedural codes such as the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC) and the Indian Evidence Act, whereas tribunals function primarily on the Principles of Natural Justice.

Part XIV-A was inserted into the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, creating provisions for Administrative Tribunals (Article 323A) and Tribunals for other matters (Article 323B).
Members of a court are strictly judicial officers, whereas tribunals consist of both judicial members and technical or administrative experts.
